column9: Audio reliability was the main problem. I experienced one-way audio, calls that remained stuck before dialing, and robotic or severely degraded outbound audio. The same problem appeared with two independent sources—Chrome WebRTC and an ElevenLabs SIP trunk—when calls reached the mobile network. Troubleshooting required significant time and many configuration changes. Some support responses did not match the actual integration; for example, I received advice about bidirectional WebSocket media streaming even though my setup used a direct SIP trunk. column8: What I like best about Telnyx CPaaS is its robust and reliable API, which has made integrating their services incredibly smooth for our specific needs. We heavily rely on their number masking feature to protect the privacy of property owners and tenants when communicating with security personnel at gated communities. This functionality ensures that personal phone numbers are never directly exposed during entry authorizations or package delivery notifications, adding a crucial layer of security and privacy for everyone involved. Furthermore, Telnyx's international SMS delivery service has been consistently dependable for our global communication requirements. The reach and reliability of their SMS platform are impressive, allowing us to efficiently send notifications and updates across borders without issue. The combination of these features – the seamless integration via their API, the effective number masking for enhanced privacy, and the reliable international SMS capabilities – makes Telnyx an invaluable CPaaS provider for our operations.
column9: While our overall experience with Telnyx CPaaS has been positive, one area that could be improved is the maintenance of their PHP SDK. We've noticed that it doesn't always seem to be kept fully up-to-date. For example, the most recent commit at the time of writing introduced a change that incorrectly set the baseApiUrl to localhost for testing purposes. This oversight wasn't removed before the commit was finalized, which means that anyone integrating the SDK currently needs to manually override this setting in their code to ensure proper functionality. While this hasn't been a critical blocker for us, it does introduce an unnecessary extra step in the integration process and suggests that the PHP SDK might not be receiving the same level of consistent attention as other aspects of their platform.
